title: Econ data sanity checks and finance sign-off action log
body:
Purpose:

Short: capture manual sanity checks performed against the cost model spreadsheets, enumerate data sources used for each input, record calibration steps taken in response to finance questions, and create an explicit action log for remaining sign-off items. This doc is the working artifact for product + finance to converge on final assumptions before we move these into the canonical cost-model workbook (sheet: "MasterEconV2").

High-level summary (current state):
- We merged infra telemetry (billing + runtime traces) with the traffic profile survey (internal) and initial customer telemetry.
- Key areas adjusted since last review: GPU hr rate (down ~6% after reserved instance negotiation), average seq length profile (median shifted from 220 to 180 tokens), and KV-cache hit assumptions (improved after cache experiment: +12% hit).
- Outstanding: amortization window for dedicated nodes, and exact rounding rules for embedding unitization that finance insists on for revenue recognition.

Data sources inventory (where each model input comes from):
- Infrastructure unit costs:
  - Source: Billing export (GCP invoice + internal cost mapping), file: billing/2025-q3-exports.csv (ingested into sheet "InfraCosts_Q3").
  - Notes: use committed use discount lines where available; exclude pass-through storage until we confirm retention window.
- Serving telemetry (latency, p99, GPU utilization):
  - Source: Observability traces (Prometheus -> BigQuery export) table: service.runtime.serving_telemetry_2025
  - Notes: sampled at 1m resolution, we aggregated to hourly then to per-model distributions to derive per-token GPU time estimate.
- Tokenization distribution (seq length):
  - Source: Sampled request corpus from hosted-api (anonymized) -> storage path s3://redwood-anon/samples/2025-09
  - Notes: we used approx 150k requests across regions; removed chat-system messages and only used user messages for generation sequences.
- Caching effectiveness (prefix / KV cache):
  - Source: cache-sim runs (dev infra), experiment id: cache-exp-2025-08-17, results in sheet "CacheSimSummary".
  - Notes: cache hit fractions were measured under steady-state synthetic replay; we applied a -5% penalty to account for warm-up effects in production.
- Quantization/throughput uplift factors:
  - Source: bench table from serving-runtime/benchmarks/quantization-2025.md (kernel-level results), PR: github.com/redwood-inference/bench/pull/92.
  - Notes: we conservatively apply the measured throughput uplift to per-token GPU time only for T4-like instances; for H100-family we use separate table.

Sanity checks performed (manual spot checks):
1) Per-token cost cross-check:
   - Calculation used: per-token GPU cost = (gpu-hr-rate / 3600) * measured-ms-per-token / 1000
   - Input snapshot: gpu-hr-rate = $2.40 (post-discount), measured-ms-per-token = 12.5 ms (model A baseline seq=128).
   - Result: per-token GPU cost = ($2.40 / 3600) * 12.5 = $0.00000833 * 12.5 = $0.0001041 (~0.0104 cents).
   - Finance sanity: aligns within 7% of the finance-expected $0.00011 after memory overhead and NVLink egress adjustments.
2) End-to-end cost vs invoice (spot check):
   - Picked 3 high-volume customer routes; simulated 30 days using traffic profiles and per-token cost -> estimated infra spend = $91,840; invoice reported (after discounts) = $95,200.
   - Gap ~3.6% accounted for by storage/egress and unmodeled control-plane CPU costs (we flagged these).
3) KV cache impact check:
   - Baseline model unit cost w/o cache = $0.00018/token; with observed 12% hit = effective cost $0.000158/token.
   - Spot-check against experimental replay: cost delta within model estimate +/- 9%.

Calibration steps taken in response to finance feedback (summary):
- Adjusted GPU hr rate to incorporate Q4 reserved commitment: updated rate table in sheet "InfraCosts_Q3" and updated formula references in MasterEconV2. Owner: Marcus Lee.
- Added explicit rounding rules for per-embedding units (ceil to nearest 1K tokens for billing math) as requested by Finance. Owner: Priya Kaur.
- Introduced a separate bucket for control-plane CPU costs (per-route apportioning) after invoice mismatch. Added sheet "ControlPlaneAlloc" and a link from MasterEconV2. Owner: Ethan Rivera.
- Introduced sensitivity columns (low/base/high) for three knobs: GPU hr rate, avg seq length, and cache hit. These are now present in MasterEconV2 col sets G:I. Owner: Lin Zhao.

Finance sign-off checklist (required artifacts):
- [ ] Canonical MasterEconV2 workbook (single source of truth) updated with final references to InfraCosts_Q3, CacheSimSummary, ControlPlaneAlloc. (owner: Marcus)
- [ ] Signed e-mail from Finance acknowledging final GPU hr rate table used (FIN-4321). (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Reconciliation notes showing <5% variance vs actual invoice for a representative month. (owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Documentation of rounding/billing unit rules for embeddings and token counting to support revenue recognition. (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Registered Confluence page with final assumption list and links to sheets (owner: Sofia)

Open questions / unresolved items (need decisions):
- Amortization window for Dedicated pool nodes: 24 months (product preference) vs finance-preferred 36 months. Impact on per-token infra amortization is ~12–15% for some SKUs. Decision required by 2025-11-10. (owner: Finance)
- Should we model customer-level SLA credits as an expected liability line in the unit economics (conservative) or treat as ad-hoc? Finance prefers conservative; product prefers ad-hoc. Need to run sensitivity scenarios and present to FP&A. (owner: Sofia + Marcus)
- Embedding billing rule: finance asks to round up embedding consumption to the nearest 1k tokens per request; product suggests aggregating per-customer per-day. Which one aligns with our billing engine and legal? Blocker for revenue recognition. (owner: Priya)

Action log (concrete next steps):
- 2025-10-20: Marcus updated InfraCosts_Q3 with negotiated rates and pushed a PR to canonical workbook. (status: done)
- 2025-10-22: Priya documented embedding rounding rules draft and added examples to "BillingNotes" sheet. (status: in_review)
- 2025-10-25: Lin added sensitivity columns and a small macro to produce low/base/high export for exec slides; needs review for formula stability. (status: in_review)
- 2025-10-27: Ethan produced reconciliation run vs August invoice and posted results under "Reconciliations/August2025". Discrepancy logged and matched to control-plane CPU now. (status: done)
- 2025-11-03: Sofia to consolidate final sign-off doc and schedule finance review meeting (target 2025-11-07). (status: assigned)

Risks & notes for reviewers:
- The token distribution sample is skewed towards English-first customers; APAC seq lengths differ by ~8% on average — we need a regional multiplier if customers are APAC-heavy.
- Benchmarks used for quantization uplift are microbenchmarks (isolated kernels). We applied a conservative 70% of measured uplift to avoid overclaiming model-level gains.
- Invoice reconciliation is currently sample-based; we should plan a full 3-month rolling reconciliation before finalizing the amortization policy.

Appendix (quick pointers to sheets and files):
- Master workbook: docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1H2x-optimize-cost-model-v2 (sheet: MasterEconV2)
- Infra costs: sheet "InfraCosts_Q3" in same workbook, tab id: InfraCosts_Q3
- Cache experiments: sheet "CacheSimSummary", workbook: docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1H2x-optimize-cache-sim
- Bench artifacts: repo github.com/redwood-inference/bench, PR#92, file bench/quantization-2025.md

If you're reviewing: please focus on the three knobs in the sensitivity sheet (GPU hr rate, avg seq length, cache hit). Flag anything that moves unit cost by >10% between low/base/high and add comments in the MasterEconV2 workbook (cell comments) so we have a clear audit trail for Finance.

-- Sofia Martinez (product-optimize)
